NEXTDC.why: Builds and leases colocation and hyperscale data centre capacity in Australia and Kuala Lumpur, including high-density liquid-to-chip capacity; AI, cloud, hyperscaler and neocloud deployments drive its contracted utilisation (740.1MW) and Forward Order Book.
NEXTDC.evidence: NEXTDC FY26 results release (08-27-2026): 'AI, cloud, hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprise, as well as ICT alliances and partners all driving strong growth in colocation and hyperscale deployments'; contracted utilisation up 202% to 740.1MW; Forward Order Book 565.1MW.

players.product: AI-ready colocation and hyperscale data centres (including high-density liquid-to-chip capacity) in Sydney, Melbourne, other Australian metros and Kuala Lumpur for cloud, AI, hyperscaler and neocloud deployments

quarterly_data.quarter: NEXTDC results presentation: FY26 Full-Year Results (08-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Results presentation: 12MW delivered at M2 Melbourne during FY26 and construction of a further 60MW of high-density liquid to chip capacity is in progress; new and existing facility expansions are increasingly using highly efficient cooling technologies, including liquid to chip.
quarterly_data.figure: 60MW liquid to chip capacity in progress at M2

quarterly_data.quarter: NEXTDC results presentation: FY26 Full-Year Results (08-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Results presentation: rapid growth in high density hyperscale billing capacity is changing the billing and revenue mix, with over 70% of billing capacity now coming from hyperscale and increasing; hyperscale developments are now targeting over 10% Yield on Cost. Cloud and AI deployments are showing strong growth in size and scale.
quarterly_data.figure: Over 70% of billing capacity from hyperscale

quarterly_data.quarter: NEXTDC results presentation: FY26 Full-Year Results (08-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Results presentation: A1 Adelaide additional 2MW and P2 Perth additional 4MW in progress to support AI deployment; KL1 Kuala Lumpur 10MW delivered, 15MW in progress and 15MW in plan; total IT power across the portfolio 3,030MW with 2,289MW uncontracted; contracted utilisation equal to 257% of built capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: Total IT power 3,030MW; contracted 257% of built capacity
